prs.author: rcdailey

prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Standalone GET SSE stream connections go idle and get dropped by reverse proxies/load balancers because no traffic is sent during idle periods; both PRs add a periodic keepalive mechanism to the same standalone GET SSE stream in packages/server/src/server/streamableHttp.ts to prevent this disconnection. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #1726 wires the keepalive timer into the existing StreamMapping struct (adds a `keepAliveTimer` field alongside the struct's existing `cleanup: () => void`), reusing the stream's established lifecycle/cleanup path. #2124 instead manages the timer via a separate local closure variable and a standalone `clearKeepAlive()` helper defined outside StreamMapping, a second, disconnected cleanup mechanism for the same resource. #1726 also exposes the interval as a configurable `keepAliveInterval` option on `WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransportOptions`, letting the interval be tuned to a deployment's specific proxy idle-timeout threshold rather than being fixed. Recommend closing #2124 and porting any test cases it has that aren't covered by #1726 onto #1726 before merge.

clusters.pick_reason: #1726 wires the keepalive timer into the existing StreamMapping struct (adds a `keepAliveTimer` field alongside the struct's existing `cleanup: () => void`), reusing the stream's established lifecycle/cleanup path. #2124 instead manages the timer via a separate local closure variable and a standalone `clearKeepAlive()` helper defined outside StreamMapping, a second, disconnected cleanup mechanism for the same resource. #1726 also exposes the interval as a configurable `keepAliveInterval` option on `WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransportOptions`, letting the interval be tuned to a deployment's specific proxy idle-timeout threshold rather than being fixed. Recommend closing #2124 and porting any test cases it has that aren't covered by #1726 onto #1726 before merge.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs patch the same Accept-header check in webStandardStreamableHttp.ts. #1996 adds an acceptsMediaType() helper that parses comma-separated media ranges and honors q=0 (explicit rejection), whereas #2046 uses a plain acceptHeader.includes('application/json') substring check with no q-value or media-range parsing — it would misclassify a header like 'application/json;q=0, text/event-stream' as accepting JSON when the client explicitly declined it. #1996's parsing is the more spec-correct implementation of the same fix.
